# Flight NCR draft: Propellant tank, 12 L titanium

**Vehicle:** KESTREL-1 · **Mission day:** 41 · **Part:** P-PROP-02 (KS1-PRP-1002 rev B) · **Status:** draft for MRB

**Symptom:** Tank pressure decay of -0.087 psi/day over 7 days, exceeding -0.030 psi/day limit, indicating potential leak

## Flight evidence

| Channel | Latest | Trend per day |
|---|---|---|
| TM-PROP-03 Tank pressure at 20 °C | 286.44 psia | -0.087 psia |

## Linked build records

| Record | Title | Status | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| NCR-001 | Isolation valve seat leakage exceeds limit after thermal cycling | open | none |
| NCR-003 | Propellant tank girth weld porosity found in radiography | dispositioned | use_as_is |

## Summary

The pressure decay of -0.087 psi/day observed in TM-PROP-03 exceeds limits and matches the leak rate from the isolation valve seat nonconformance NCR-001, which was flown as “Closed for flight: flight valve accepted”. This leak projects only 29 m/s of delta-v remaining at end-of-life, 91 m/s short of the 120 m/s required by REQ-SYS-002. The recommended operational mitigation is to reduce thrust setpoint by 10 % and increase telemetry monitoring to every 2 hours pending operator approval.

## Recommended disposition and actions

- **Rationale**: The observed pressure trend is consistent with a qualifying valve seat leak (NCR-001) that threatens to leave the spacecraft 91 m/s short of its delta-v budget, risking mission success.
- **Risks**: If the leak continues, propellant will become stranded below 100 psia feed pressure, eliminating usable delta-v and potentially ending the mission prematurely.
- **Next steps**:
  - Await operator decision at the Svalbard pass (T+140 min) on the proposed propulsion procedure (thrust -10 %, telemetry every 2 h).
  - Upon approval, implement the procedure and begin 2-hourly TM-PROP-03 checks.
  - Track pressure trend; if decay persists, prepare a formal flight NCR for the next build and consider further operational constraints (e.g., reduced duty cycle).
</executive_summary>

_Generated by SpaceGrade Agent from flight telemetry and the build pedigree. Synthetic data._

**Diagnosis**: TM-PROP-03 shows a tank-pressure decay of -0.088 psi/day (latest 286.44 psia) over the past 7 days, exceeding the -0.030 psi/day limit [TM-PROP-03]. The trend matches the helium-leak rate inferred from the qualification valve seat leak recorded in NCR-001 (3.2e-4 scc/s GHe) which was dispositioned for flight as “Closed for flight: flight valve accepted” [NCR-001]. No propulsion activity occurred in the window, so the decay is indicative of a slow leak rather than usage.

**Why the build record mattered**: Without NCR-001 the spec-sheet model would treat the pressure trend as an unknown cause, providing no basis for a leak-rate estimate or delta-v projection. With NCR-001, the observed trend translates to an equivalent helium leak of 0.00032 sccs, projecting only 29 m/s of delta-v remaining at end-of-life versus the 120 m/s required (REQ-SYS-002), a shortfall of 91 m/s [TM-PROP-03][REQ-SYS-002]. This quantitative link changes the prognosis from nominal performance to a significant mission-impacting deficit.

**For the operator**:  
*At the next pass (Svalbard, T+140 min)*  
- Review and decide on the proposed propulsion procedure: reduce thrust setpoint by 10 % and increase tank-pressure telemetry cadence to every 2 hours.  
- Verify the procedure fields are correct and note the delta-v shortfall check (29 m/s remaining vs 120 m/s required).  

*Afterwards*  
- Monitor TM-PROP-03 every 2 hours to confirm pressure trend stabilises or further decays.  
- Re-compute remaining delta-v and update the mission plan if the leak persists.  
- Document the outcome and, if needed, file a formal flight NCR for the next build.
